title:
RT by @hwchase17: Building agents (like software) is a deeply iterative process --> this is why we try to supply as much easy to use tooling and infra as possible so builders can start on their agent improvement journey asap

storing and understanding traces is the fastest onramp to understand agent behavior and detect where your agents are messing up today.  things like:
- what are people asking my agents?
- what actions are resulting in failed tool calls?
- what kind of work is expensive to run today for our agents?  can it be cheaper?

once you mine trace data, you can "do something" to improve your agents
- harness engineering
- making evals
- swapping models
- post-training

these are all levers we have to improve agent dev, but pretty much all of this is downstream of gathering and understanding traces at scale

ship a v1
turn on tracing
understand the traces and errors
experiments
loop

RT by @pmarca: There was nothing more crazy than the remote monitoring arms race during COVID.

In real time I went from non-proctored exams to being forced to use webapps that tracked all the activity of my computer to take a physics test for college.

Then like 3 weeks later it became scanning your entire room and forced to use a webcam. 

To get around this I knew people that would blue-light glasses because it would reflect the screen and the camera couldn't track their eye movements. 

In response professors asked kids to not use blue light glasses, so the kids would get doctors notes for "blue light sensitivity." 

Same thing with key monitoring. What a surreal time.
